The *Madhudāyakattheraapadāna* is a Pali verse text included within the *Therāpadāna* section of the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [SuttaCentral]. While SuttaCentral records no English title, it notes five translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No independent parallels are curated by SuttaCentral, but automated textual analysis indicates substantial shared phrasing within the Pali tradition and across Buddhist literature [DharmaNexus]. According to DharmaNexus, the text shares 162 passages with 24 other Pali works, most prominently with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), where a continuous block (§0.3–17.4) closely matches commentary segments with a 0.92 similarity score [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits standard formulaic reuse with numerous other poems in the *Therāpadāna*, including the *Pānadhidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 481), *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8), *Sabbadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 401), and *Madhumaṁsadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 416) [DharmaNexus]. Additionally, DharmaNexus aligns passages of the text with sections of the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu*, although these machine alignments reflect shared terminology or narrative motifs rather than established direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
